VIII.|TO THE ROMANES.|401}}</noinclude>of the sonnes of God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}}† For the creature is made subiect to vanitie, not vvilling, but for him that made it subiect in hope: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=21}}† because the creature also it self shal be deliuered from the seruitude of corruption, into the libertie of the glorie of the children of God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=22}}† For vve knovv that euery creature groneth, and trauaileth euen til novv. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=23}}† And not only it, but vve also our selues hauing the first fruites of the spirit, vve also grone vvithin our selues, expecting the adoption of the sonnes of God, the redemption of our body.⊣ {{verse|chapter=8|verse=24}}† For {{sup|‖}} by hope vve are saued. But hope that is seen, is not hope. for that vvhich a man seeth, vvherfore doth he hope it? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=25}}† But if vve hope for that vvhich vve see not: vve expect by patience. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=26}}† And in like maner also the Spirit helpeth our infirmitie. For, vvhat vve should pray as vve ought, vve knovv not: but the Spirit him self requesteth for vs vvith gronings vnspeakeable. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=27}}† And he that searcheth the hartes, knovveth vvhat {{sup|‖}} the Spirit desireth: because according to God he requesteth for the sainctes. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=28}}† And vve knovv that to them that loue God, al things cooperate vnto good, to such as according to purpose are called to be sainctes. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=29}}† For vvhom he hath forknowen, he hath also predestinated to be made conformable to the image of his sonne: that he might be the first-borne in many brethren. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=30}}† And {{sup|‖}} vvhom he hath predestinated: them also he hath called. and vvhom he hath called: them also he hath iustified. and vvhom he hath iustified: them also hath he glorified. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=31}}† What shal vve then say to these things? If God be for vs, vvho is against vs? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=32}}† He that spared not also his ovvne sonne, but for vs al deliuered him: hovv hath he not also vvith him giuen vs al things? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=33}}† Who shal accuse against the elect of God? God that iustifieth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=34}}† Who is he that shal condemne? Christ {{sc|Iesvs}} that died, yea that is risen also againe, vvho is on the right hand of God, vvho also maketh intercession for vs. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=35}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Epistle for S. Ignatius Febr. 1.}}∷ Who then shal separate vs from the charitie of Christ? tribulation? or distresse? or famine? or nakednes? or danger? or persecution? or the svvord? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=36}}† (as it is vvritten, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 43, 22.''}}* ''For vve are killed for thy sake al the day: vve are esteemed as sheepe of slaughter''.) {{verse|chapter=8|verse=37}}† But in al these things we ouercome because of him that hath loued vs. c {{verse|chapter=8|verse=38}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''πέπεισμαι γὰρ''.}}∷ For {{sup|‖}} I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor Angels, nor Principalities, nor Povvers, neither things present, nor things to come, neither might, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=39}}† nor height, nor depth, nor other creature, shal be able to<noinclude>{{rh||Eee|separate}}</noinclude>
